correctness.rationale: The algebraic deduction is correct. The 2026 sqrt-Delta-fine source states that such a ring is simple and that every full matrix ring remains sqrt-Delta-fine. For a nonzero unital simple ring the Jacobson radical is zero. Using Leroy--Matczuk's matrix identity Delta(M_n(S))=J(M_n(S))=M_n(J(S)) for n at least two gives Delta(M_n(R))=0, hence sqrt(Delta(M_n(R))) is exactly the nilpotent cone. The matrix closure then makes every nonzero matrix a unit plus a nilpotent. The E_11 corner computation is standard and correctly yields the Morita/full-corner consequence.

originality.rationale: The submitted theorem is a direct composition of published results. The 2026 primary source explicitly states both simplicity of every sqrt-Delta-fine ring and closure under M_n for every n. Leroy--Matczuk supply the matrix identity reducing Delta(M_n(R)) to the Jacobson radical for n at least two. Once these are combined, J(R)=0 follows immediately from simplicity and the nilpotent conclusion is just the definition of the radical root. Thus the matrix-fineness statement is a routine corollary of two published theorems; the Morita sentence is the standard full-corner contrapositive. Under implication-based originality this is covered even if the exact corollary was not printed verbatim.
